items.title: Scott Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe,Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: And at Blues Alley I heard Earl Hines and Clark Terry and Lockjaw Davis and Dizzy Gillespie... I would sit right in front with a glass of water, and just take a lesson.

ctx.x: You had a pretty good experience in high school and so forth with jazz?

Well I was a jazz freak and I converted a few of my closest friends to being jazz freaks, and some of them had driver’s licenses before I did, so I was able to cajole them into driving into Washington D.C. — I grew up in Virginia. And we’d go to Blues Alley. And at Blues Alley I heard Earl Hines and Clark Terry and Lockjaw Davis and Dizzy Gillespie, Bobby Hackett, Zoot Sims — a lot of great, great musicians. And I would sit right in front with a glass of water, and just take a lesson. It was great. I did that as…
little bit of a struggle. So when I finally got to college, Berklee College of Music in Boston, suddenly I was surrounded with people that wanted to do what I was trying to do.
